references.text: God's covenant with Abraham, where He promises the land from the River of Egypt to the great river Euphrates, including the land of the Amorites - this is the same territory described in Deuteronomy 1:7
The description of the promised land flowing with milk and honey, including the land of the Canaanites - the same geographical area mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:7
God's promise regarding the borders of the land from the Salt Sea to the Philistine sea and from the wilderness to the river (Euphrates) - parallel to the border description in Deuteronomy 1:7
The spies' report on the peoples in the land: the Amalekites in the Negev, the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites in the mountains - the same geographical areas as in Deuteronomy 1:7
A detailed description of Canaan's borders that Israel was to take over - supplementing the shorter border description in Deuteronomy 1:7
Repetition of the promise regarding the land's borders from the wilderness to Lebanon and from Euphrates to the Western Sea - almost identical to Deuteronomy 1:7
Joshua's description of the remaining land from the wilderness and Lebanon to the great river Euphrates - fulfillment of the promise in Deuteronomy 1:7
Description of the kings in the mountains, in the lowlands (Shephelah), and by the coast of the great sea toward Lebanon - the same geographical division as in Deuteronomy 1:7
Summary of the territories of the defeated kings in the mountains, the lowlands, the Jordan Valley, and the Negev - the areas mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:7
During Solomon's reign, he ruled over all kingdoms from Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to Egypt's border - fulfillment of the land promise in Deuteronomy 1:7
